TODAY IS 2026-09-29. Every "passed" or "expiring" judgement is against that date.

THE AGENCY THIS AUDIT IS ABOUT: Oregon DEQ
Only this agency. Another regulator's documents are listed at the end as titles only and
are not yours to judge here.

WHO THIS COMPANY IS
  Name: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
  Industry: chemical manufacturing (recorded as chemical-manufacturing)
  Address: Portland, Oregon
Their sites:
  - Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210, Portland, Oregon (primary)

DOCUMENTS ON FILE FOR OREGON DEQ — 1

  --- Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit
      id: 69bbc42a-9a5c-4776-80d9-ae819d0ff87d
      file: 02-acdp-chemical.pdf
      kind: permit · status: expiring · shown as: expiring
      the document's own date: 2021-09-01 (issued)
      the date that matters: 2026-11-15 (expiry)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is a Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit issued by Oregon DEQ for Cascade Specialty Chemicals' chemical storage and repackaging operations with vapor control at their Portland facility. The permit authorizes operation of two wet scrubbers, four solvent storage tanks, and related equipment, subject to specific operating conditions, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations set by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT OBLIGES THEM TO KEEP DOING (14), read out of the document itself:
        · 1.1 — Operate sources in compliance with permit conditions and DEQ rules
            the evidence you would expect to see: Demonstration that all operations conform to this permit and applicable OAR 340-216 rules
        · 1.2 — Permit expires November 15, 2026; operation after expiration without renewal is a violation
            the evidence you would expect to see: Valid renewal permit or evidence that a timely renewal application was submitted before July 18, 2026
        · 1.3 — Submit complete permit renewal application by July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiration)
            the evidence you would expect to see: Confirmation of application submission to DEQ; applicant may continue operation if timely and complete application is submitted
        · 1.4 — Notify DEQ in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership or modification that increases emissions
            the evidence you would expect to see: Written notice to DEQ prior to ownership change or source modification
        · 3.1 — Maintain scrubber pressure drop within 2.0 to 6.0 inches of water column when operating
            the evidence you would expect to see: Daily scrubber log recording pressure drop readings for each operating day
        · 3.2 — Inspect scrubber components (pump, nozzles, packing, mist eliminator) quarterly
            the evidence you would expect to see: Quarterly inspection records in scrubber log showing date, inspector name, and any corrective actions
        · 3.3 — Replace carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least annually or when breakthrough detected
            the evidence you would expect to see: Records of all carbon replacements with dates; weekly detector-tube checks at C-1 outlet
        · 3.4 — Limit visible emissions to 20 percent opacity for no more than 3 minutes per hour
            the evidence you would expect to see: Opacity monitoring records; documentation of any exceedances and corrective actions
        · 4.1 — Submit annual report by February 15 covering previous calendar year
            the evidence you would expect to see: Annual report to DEQ including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates, and excess emission events
        · 4.2 — Submit semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 for January-June period
            the evidence you would expect to see: Semi-annual report to DEQ for first half of calendar year
        · 4.3 — Maintain all permit records for at least five years
            the evidence you would expect to see: Accessible records available for DEQ inspection on request
        · 5.1 — Take all reasonable steps to minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction
            the evidence you would expect to see: Procedures in place to stop associated repackaging line until scrubber is repaired
        · 5.2 — Notify DEQ within 24 hours of any permit deviation by telephone or email
            the evidence you would expect to see: Telephone or email notification within 24 hours; written report within 15 days describing deviation, cause, duration, and corrective action
        · 6.2 — Pay annual permit fee by due date on invoice
            the evidence you would expect to see: Proof of payment of annual permit fee to DEQ
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (4):
        · Permit expires; continued operation requires valid renewal — 2026-11-15
        · Submit annual report to Department — 2027-02-15 (recurring)
        · Submit complete permit renewal application — 2026-07-18
        · Submit semi-annual monitoring report — 2027-07-31 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (2) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Renewal Application Submission Status — The renewal deadline (July 18, 2026) has passed. The document does not confirm whether a renewal application was timely submitted, which is critical to the company's ability to legally continue operations
        · Toxic Air Contaminant Permit Addendum (if applicable) — For Standard ACDPs, DEQ may require a Toxic Air Contaminant Permit Addendum under OAR 340-216-0069 upon renewal if toxic air contaminants are involved

FACTS THIS COMPANY HAS CONFIRMED, ACROSS EVERYTHING THEY HOLD
Each was read in a document and then confirmed by a person. Nothing a reading merely
proposed is here — an unconfirmed proposal is a question, not a fact.
  (nothing confirmed yet)

EVERYTHING ELSE THIS COMPANY HOLDS — 4, TITLES AND DATES ONLY
Listed so you can say what is NOT among them. You have not been shown their contents and
must not describe what is in them.
  - Emergency Action Plan · policy · gaps_found · 2021-02-01
  - Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log · record · gaps_found · 2026-09-18
  - Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log · record · recorded · 2026-09-17
  - Safety Data Sheet for Sodium Hydroxide Solution, 50% · supplier_document · not_judged · 2024-03-18
